name: Founding of Rome
description: The city of Rome is founded by Romulus and Remus on the Palatine Hill.

name: Roman Republic Established
description: The Roman Republic is established after the overthrow of the Roman Kingdom.

name: Roman conquest of Italy
description: Rome successfully conquers the Italian peninsula, gaining control over the entire region.

name: First Punic War
description: Rome engages in a conflict with Carthage over control of Sicily and the western Mediterranean.

name: Second Punic War
description: Hannibal, the Carthaginian general, leads an invasion of Italy, causing major losses for Rome.

name: Roman conquest of Greece
description: Rome conquers Greece, bringing it under Roman control.

name: Third Punic War
description: Rome destroys Carthage, bringing an end to the Carthaginian civilization.

name: Roman Empire Established
description: Octavian becomes the first Roman Emperor, taking the title of Augustus.

name: Construction of Roman Colosseum
description: The construction of the iconic Roman Colosseum is completed.

name: Roman invasion of Britain
description: The Roman Empire invades and begins the conquest of Britain.

name: Destruction of Pompeii
description: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius leads to the destruction of the city of Pompeii.

name: Roman Empire divides into East and West
description: The Roman Empire splits into the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Western Roman Empire falls to various invasions and internal conflicts.

name: Justinian's reign
description: Emperor Justinian I rules over the Byzantine Empire and attempts to reconquer the Western Roman Empire.

name: Theodoric the Great
description: Theodoric the Great becomes king of the Ostrogoths, ruling over Italy.

name: Coronation of Charlemagne
description: Charlemagne is crowned as the first Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III.

name: Byzantine Iconoclasm
description: The Byzantine Empire enters a period of iconoclasm, with the destruction of religious icons.

name: Great Fire of Rome
description: A massive fire breaks out in Rome, causing widespread destruction.

name: Battle of Actium
description: Octavian defeats Mark Antony and Cleopatra, securing his position as the sole ruler of Rome.

name: Reign of Nero
description: Emperor Nero rules Rome and is known for his extravagant lifestyle and persecution of Christians.

name: Constantinople becomes the new capital of the Roman Empire
description: Constantine the Great establishes Constantinople (current day Istanbul) as the new capital of the Roman Empire.

name: Edict of Milan
description: Emperors Constantine and Licinius issue the Edict of Milan, granting religious tolerance to Christians in the Roman Empire.

name: Fall of Constantinople
description: The city of Constantinople falls to the Ottoman Empire, marking the end of the Byzantine Empire.

name: Roman aqueducts built
description: The construction of the vast Roman aqueducts begins, providing a reliable water supply to cities across the empire.

name: Roman road network expanded
description: The Roman Empire extensively develops an advanced system of roads, facilitating trade and communication.

name: Pax Romana
description: The Roman Empire experiences a period of relative peace and stability, known as the Pax Romana.

name: Julius Caesar's assassination
description: Julius Caesar is assassinated, leading to a power struggle and ultimately the downfall of the Roman Republic.

name: Christianity becomes the official religion of the Roman Empire
description: Emperor Theodosius I declares Christianity as the official religion of the Roman Empire.

name: Roman expansion into Gaul
description: Rome conquers Gaul (modern-day France), extending its control over Western Europe.

name: Reign of Trajan
description: Emperor Trajan oversees a period of territorial expansion and major public building projects.

name: Roman law codified
description: Emperor Justinian I institutes a comprehensive codification of Roman law known as the Corpus Juris Civilis.

name: Roman baths constructed
description: The Romans construct elaborate public baths, places for relaxation, socializing, and hygiene.

name: Reign of Marcus Aurelius
description: Marcus Aurelius serves as the last of the Five Good Emperors, known for his Stoic philosophy.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

name: Roman conquest of Egypt
description: Egypt is conquered by Rome, bringing it under Roman rule.

name: Reign of Diocletian
description: Diocletian becomes Emperor of Rome and initiates major reforms in an attempt to stabilize the empire.

name: Roman law expanded to incorporate non-Roman citizens
description: The Romans extend their legal system to incorporate non-Roman citizens, providing them with legal protections.

name: Barbarian invasions of the Roman Empire
description: The Roman Empire faces invasions from Germanic tribes such as the Visigoths and Vandals.

name: Roman conquest of Dacia
